body: Marking as high-priority since apparently it does not work with default options (i.e. `async = false`).
It should only hide the body temporarily in "sync" mode, which should probably be the default.

Okay, I've tracked this down.

The problem is that less.refresh() returns a Promise, and that Promise is not always resolved. The way that it gets resolved is by firing the callback from the loadStyleSheets function. However, the callback is not fired if you _don't have any stylesheets_.

Now, I don't disagree that the body perhaps shouldn't hide on the event of this error (and it's not good practice to create Promises that sometimes don't resolve), but the plain fact is that you're calling Less.js on a page with no Less. So it's a user error more than a Less error. So, at the most, this would be a low-priority bug, since in normal usage, it doesn't look like this error would occur.
Re-marking as ~~low~~ medium priority (the way the code is written is still error-prone) unless there's an example of this occurring with Less styles.

> So, at the most, this would be a low-priority bug, since in normal usage, it doesn't look like this error would occur.

It also does not work with [inline only](http://jsbin.com/hifibubiya/edit?html,output) Less styles, i.e. it breaks not only weird incomplete examples.
@seven-phases-max Ah, okay, bumping back up to high. I'll try to take a look at this soon.

@matthew-dean Actually I'm using it in an online Less compiler (http://ecomfe.github.io/est/fiddle/) so it's obviously not a user error to have no Less stylesheets in the page. I'm currently working this around by setting `onReady = false` (which is okay in my use case).

> I'm currently working this around by setting `onReady = false` (which is okay in my use case).

A less intrusive workaround would be simply `<script>less = {async: true};</script>`.

> so it's obviously not a user error to have no Less stylesheets in the page

Yes, my mistake.
@seven-phases-max So just to be clear, Promises are never fulfilled with inline styles either?

> Promises are never fulfilled with inline styles either?

I can't really confirm "never" (since this requires infinite tests :), but from basic tests it appears like so.
